spec.purpose: Compare original four-IU8 signed16 core products with two IU8 matrices and one zero-C FP16 centered cross-term matrix. S equals signed high byte plus unsigned low byte minus128 and lies in[-256,254]. Nearest-integer recovery uses the explicit empirical-model85/256 error bound. Inline and separately prepared36-byte centered encodings are checked. Every exact integer partial, rounded cross term and reconstructed signed16 dot is compared with an independent CPU sum. All65536 input encodings, full GPU row encodings, immutable arrays and guards are checked. One warmup and three rotated samples verify every sequence output; original canonical carries, BF16 exceptions, model load, inference and product performance are not exercised.

decision: Keep this arithmetic experiment isolated. At 256 groups, original/inline/prepared medians are 0.3721/1.5699/0.5425 ms, before the separately measured 5.2071 ms prepared-data cost. Both candidates are slower. The result does not justify full-QK integration or a product performance claim.
implementation: For signed16 x=256*h+l, use signed high h and unsigned low l, and exactly representable FP16 s=h+l-128 in [-256,254]. Two IU8 matrices produce HH and LL. A zero-C FP16 matrix estimates SS; native nearest-integer conversion recovers SS under the conditional absolute bound 85/256. The cross term is SS-HH-LL+128*(sumSA+sumSB)+262144, then the full dot is 65536*HH+256*cross+LL. One variant prepares inline; the other uses a separate 36-byte row with 16 FP16 values and an int32 sum, alongside the original 32-byte row.
scope: The native FP16 combined sum differs from its mathematical integer in 279356 cells per variant, with maximum absolute error 0.0234375. Nearest-integer values and full reconstructions agree with independent CPU int64 dots everywhere in this finite fixture. The rational 85/256 bound is conditional on the observed native pair model, not a universal hardware proof. Prepared rows, immutable inputs and redzones are fully checked. Sequence timings have one warmup and three rotated, fully verified measurements per variant. Preparation is measured separately and excluded from sequence timers. Canonical exponent alignment, carry normalization, BF16 exceptions and model traffic are absent, so these are arithmetic cost diagnostics, not q8192 or inference acceptance.
